_about: Teaching text for Module 2. The library, its properties and 3D shapes are real (library.json); the docking-style score is mock.

scenarios.text: You have a known drug (celecoxib) and want other compounds that look or are shaped like it.
scenarios.why: With a known active you can search for compounds that resemble it in 2D or 3D.

scenarios.text: You have the 3D structure of the target protein but no known inhibitors.
scenarios.why: Without a reference drug, you can dock compounds into the pocket and rank how well they fit.

scenarios.text: Many of the million compounds are far too big, too greasy or too polar to ever become oral drugs.
scenarios.why: Property filters such as Lipinski's rule of five remove compounds that are unlikely to be absorbed, very cheaply.

scenarios.text: Docking gives you 100 promising compounds, but the lab can only test 10 and many look alike.
scenarios.why: Choosing a varied, inspected set (and dropping assay-interference scaffolds) is the last step before testing.

prepare.item: Diclofenac sodium: the drug written as a salt with Na⁺
prepare.detail: The file contains two pieces: the drug and a sodium ion.
prepare.why: Strip the counter-ion and keep the drug. The sodium is not part of what binds the target.
prepare.bad: A free sodium ion confuses the 3D generation and the scoring.

prepare.item: (S)-ibuprofen when racemic ibuprofen is already in the library
prepare.detail: Same compound, one stereoisomer written separately.
prepare.why: Remove or merge duplicates, otherwise the same compound is counted twice and the hit list is inflated.
prepare.bad: Duplicates take two places in the ranking and bias the results.

prepare.item: Benzylidene rhodanine, which is flagged as a PAINS scaffold
prepare.detail: A substructure that often looks active in many assays for the wrong reasons.
prepare.why: Flag or remove PAINS before screening. They are frequent false positives and waste lab time.
prepare.bad: It may rank high but turn out to be an assay artefact.

prepare.item: Carboxylic acids (for example ibuprofen) drawn in the neutral form
prepare.detail: At body pH (about 7.4) these acids lose their proton.
prepare.why: Assign the charge state for the pH. The carboxylate, not the neutral acid, is what meets the protein, for example the arginine at the entrance of the COX-2 channel.
prepare.bad: The wrong charge changes hydrogen bonds and electrostatics in the score.

prepare.detail: The library came as sketches with no 3D coordinates.
prepare.why: Generate realistic 3D conformers (and minimise them). Shape and docking methods need 3D.
prepare.bad: A flat molecule cannot be overlaid or docked sensibly.

prepare.item: A chiral compound with the 3D configuration not specified
prepare.detail: Naproxen is the (S) form, but the entry did not say which.
prepare.why: Assign or enumerate the stereoisomers. Different mirror images can bind very differently.
prepare.bad: You may dock the wrong mirror image and get a misleading rank.

prepare.item: A 3,000 Da peptide in a small-molecule library
prepare.detail: Far larger than a typical drug.
prepare.why: Remove compounds outside the size range the method and the project were designed for.
prepare.bad: It slows the run and gives unreliable scores.

prepare.item: A compound for which no 3D structure could be generated
prepare.detail: The program failed on an unusual ring system.
prepare.why: Drop it (and note it). Do not keep a compound with no valid structure.
prepare.bad: Broken structures give meaningless scores or stop the run.

prepare.detail: Metal complexes are not handled well by standard docking programs.
prepare.why: Remove or treat separately with a method designed for metals.
prepare.bad: Standard force fields and scoring functions give unreliable results for metals.

prepare.item: Piroxicam written as one of several possible tautomers
prepare.detail: The keto and enol forms interconvert.
prepare.why: Generate the likely tautomers (or choose the dominant one) so the best form is screened.
prepare.bad: Screening only an unlikely form can hide a real hit.

nextSteps.text: Inspect poses and interactions of the selected compounds in the pocket.
Check ADME and drug-likeness of the selected compounds.
Buy or make the compounds and test them in a lab assay.
Report them as confirmed COX-2 inhibitors.
Skip testing because the ranks are good.
